claim_overlays.source_scope: NPS top-up eligibility and 119-month maximum supported; projected increase remains case only.
Illustrative return and future distribution rates are not promised; compare total return and longevity.
Consider guaranteed income vs volatility, liquidity, mortality, benefit rules, personal NPS estimate.
Not a universal optimal order; emergency cash, expected pension, liquidity, and eligibility matter.
Personal case, no general recommendation to defer consumption.
At 7% nominal annual with monthly compounding: 7 years≈KRW32.40m; 10 years≈KRW51.93m. Correct duration label; risk not guaranteed.
Applicable to eligible pension deferral; not equivalent to 7.2% invested return; tax, health contribution, survivor, inflation and missed payments matter.
Needs lifetime cash flow, survival, discount rate, taxes and year-by-year timing before choosing.
Separate flat KRW15m tax-choice threshold from account's formulaic pension-withdrawal limit and outside-pension treatment.
Does not apply identically to all pension payments, tax-excluded basis, deferred retirement income; simplistic total 16.5% cap is not universal.
Decision principle is plausible but must include market risk, withdrawal sustainability and marginal tax interactions.
Not a recommendation to maximize returns irrespective of risk; compare risk-adjusted after-tax outcomes.
Documentation of tax-excluded basis is necessary; use current law and provider account ledger.
Statutory order: tax-excluded first, deferred retirement income next, other taxable amounts thereafter; ISA transfers require individual tax-credit checks.
A distribution reduces NAV; 6% is not a guaranteed total return, and tax-free draw only while confirmed tax-excluded source remains.
Not all future distributions remain tax-free indefinitely; must track remaining source basis and account statement.
ETF legal subtype, derivatives, distribution, pension account source and timing change result; avoid treating every ETF identically.
Account-location choice conditional on asset mix, available products, liquidity, loss offset, costs and constraints.
A cited 6.5%-7.5% guaranteed rate cannot be inferred for any actual contract; verify coverage, credited rate, surrender schedule, insurer risk.
A hypothetical 5% insurance guarantee is not universal and 10% equity return is not assured; obtain contract and fee facts.
Eligibility at reopening/extension, transaction friction, asset sale, tax timing, future law and client objectives matter.
Tax netting applies to eligible ISA profits/losses; account type and applicable nettable instruments should be checked, no general forever-loss carryforward claim.
Law confirms thresholds; frequency of renewal depends on eligibility, account return profile and transfer friction; do not force three-year rollover.

quantitative_corrections.finding: 300,000 KRW monthly at 7% nominal yearly monthly compounding: 7yr 32,399,694 KRW, 10yr 51,925,442 KRW. About 51m at 7yr in source transcript is inconsistent.
750,000 KRW monthly x 20y =180m paid in; ISA 100m x 4=400m transferred. Total 580m contribution/transfer before claimed tax credits; cannot equate ~800m end value with tax-excluded principal.
4m KRW/month x 16y=768m, exceeding 580m contribution and ISA transfer example; non-taxable 16-year assertion unsupported; must track actual credit-used basis.
800m x 6% /12=4m KRW/month is arithmetic only. The cashflow is not guaranteed and can erode NAV.
18m KRW /250k KRW added NPS monthly=72 months after pension starts, not 6 years from top-up.
